item.title: UPDATE: CINEMETROPOLIS Advance Digital Download Out Now, Official Release Date June 14
item.dc:creator: Geo
item.description: Cinemetropolis advance digital download out now. Official release date: June 14.
item.content:encoded:
The official Cinemetropolis release date is June 14. But everyone who pledged to get the advance digital copy on our  kickstarter campaign began receiving the download links on May 15. We’re overwhelmed by the initial feedback and appreciate all the contributions and critiques. If you pledged but have not yet received your link, or if you’re having problems with the download, please send us an email describing the issue.

We’re about to roll out the first wave of video projects beginning with a music video for Fou Lee and the Slick Watts short film premiere. More to come in the summertime, followed by a national tour in the Fall.

AND if you’re in Seattle June 17/18, hit up our record release party at Neumos (VIP party on June 15)!

If you got the album, let us and the world know what you think! We read it all.

item.title: WE GOT SIGNED! THANKS FOR MAKING CINEMETROPOLIS A REALITY
item.dc:creator: Hollis
item.description: We made the call. You overwhelmingly responded. On March 6, Blue Scholars launched a Kickstarter campaign to help fund the release of our next album, Cinemetropolis. Our goal was $25,000, which we reached in just over one week. The… More
item.content:encoded:
We made the call. You overwhelmingly responded. On March 6, Blue Scholars launched a Kickstarter campaign to help fund the release of our next album, Cinemetropolis. Our goal was $25,000, which we reached in just over one week. The campaign ended after 45 days on April 21, with a final total of $62,371 raised from 2,242 people. Daaaang.

This was way more than we expected and confirms one thing we’ve suspected all along: we have the filthiest fans in the universe. With your contributions, we’re hella pleased to announce that Cinemetropolis is on its way, with the first round of video projects and new merch already in production. The album itself will drop on June 14, with two shows to celebrate the release in Seattle, June 17 and 18 at Neumos. Now, on to your questions:

When will I get my advance digital copy?
Those who pledged to get the advance digital copy will receive a one-time download link via e-mail on May 15.

When will I get my CD/Vinyl/Poster?
The CDs, vinyl and posters will be released to the public and delivered to people who pledged on June 14. The deluxe package CD will be available in July (see below).

When will I get my limited edition deluxe package CD?
Due to the awesome nature of its packaging, including a photo and lyric booklet, the deluxe package CD will be coming later in July.

Oh no, I missed the deadline! Can I still pledge?
Unfortunately, no. Kickstarter freezes the campaign after the deadline, and is currently processing all payments. But sit tight for the launch of our new web store on BlueScholars.com, where you will be able to purchase digital and hard copies of the album, as well as items from the Cinemetropolis product line. (Yes, including the snazzglasses!)

item.title: “SLICK WATTS” Short Film Premiere – May 18
item.dc:creator: Geo
item.description: SLICK WATTS directed by Sonicsgate. Seattle premiere: Wednesday, May 18th 8pm at SIFF Cinema!
item.content:encoded:
As we’re ticking down the final hours of the Cinemetropolis kickstarter campaign, we’d like to announce the arrival of the first short film spawned from the album: Slick Watts, directed by Jason Reid and the Sonicsgate team, starring Blue Scholars and the OG himself, Slick Watts, featuring the song Slick Watts.

You can catch the premiere screening of the short in Seattle on Wednesday, May 18th 8pm at SIFF Cinema as a preview for the narrative film series Every Day is a Journey.

Big thanks to Sonicsgate and The Watts Foundation for collaborating on this project. More info to come.

item.title: NEW SNAZZGLASSES & LAST CALL FOR KICKSTARTER
item.dc:creator: Hollis
item.description: Six weeks ago, Blue Scholars announced plans to sign with the people for the release of Cinemetropolis, and we have been overwhelmed by the support fans have shown for the project since then! Thanks to you, we have… More
item.content:encoded:
Six weeks ago, Blue Scholars announced plans to sign with the people for the release of Cinemetropolis, and we have been overwhelmed by the support fans have shown for the project since then! Thanks to you, we have raised more than double our $25,000 goal on Kickstarter, money that has already helped us wrap two video shoots, finalize the album packaging, and roll out new Blue Scholars merchandise.

Only two more days are left in the Kickstarter campaign for Cinemetropolis, which ends Thursday, April 21 at 9:30 pm PDT. Don’t sleep on your only chance to pre-order a copy of Cinemetropolis before its official release date on June 14. We added another new gift for people who haven’t pledged yet: for only $20 you can get a snazzy set of Blue Scholars sunglasses, plus an advance digital copy of the album!

Kickstarter will also be the only way to get your hands on some other one-of-a-kind Cinemetropolis gifts, including limited-edition vinyl, exclusive posters, tickets to a secret Blue Scholars concert in Seattle, or even your name in the album packaging. (And if you want the sunglasses but already made a pledge, they will be available when our new online store launches. More details coming soon…)

item.title: NEW TRACK: JOHN DELOREAN
item.dc:creator: Sabzi
item.description: New Blue Scholars track "John Delorean," an outtake from Cinemetropolis.
item.content:encoded:
Geo and I were having a discussion the other day about super powers: If you could have just one super power, what would it be?

Like a child, I said “I’d be able to fly!” and then I grinned hella big. Geo shook his head and said “Word? Well, I’d have the ability of time travel.”

“Why?” I asked.

“Think about it,” he said. “With time travel, you actually have the capacity to secure any other super power you wanted. For example, if you wanted to fly, you could just travel to a future time where personal flying technology was developed and bring it back. Now you have the ability to fly AND the ability to travel through time.”

After hearing this explanation I changed my answer to time travel as well.

“Also,” he continued with a chuckle, “you could hear a really dope song and then go back 4 months and just write and release it before that artist did hahaha.”

This was funny to me. “You sound like you’ve thought about time travel a lot.”

“I have,” he replied. “I even wrote a song about it. Here.”

“Oh snap. We should put this out.”

“Sure, and your email could basically be a recap of this conversation.”

“Hey, great idea.”

item.title: VIDEO: Blue Scholars Live on Knocksteady
item.dc:creator: Geo
item.description: A recap video from our in studio performance and interview with Knocksteady TV.
item.content:encoded:
In between the Pomona College and UC Irvine Shows last week, we got an invitation from Dumbfoundead and the Knocksteady crew to come to their studio in downtown L.A. for a live performance and interview. Here’s a recap video from Knocksteady TV including a performance of “Seijun Suzuki,” a cut featuring Thig Natural of The Physics off the upcoming Cinemetropolis record.

Some photos from the trip. Shot with the Polaroid Land Camera 230 shown in the opening shots of the video.

item.title: NOW AVAILABLE: LIMITED EDITION CINEMETROPOLIS 2-LP VINYL, RELEASE DATE ANNOUNCEMENT
item.dc:creator: Geo
item.description: You spoke, we listened, and yes: we will be pressing the next album, Cinemetropolis, on wax for all you vinyl heads out there.
item.content:encoded:
You spoke, we listened, and yes: we will be pressing the next album, Cinemetropolis, on wax for all you vinyl heads out there.

We’ve added a couple new pledge tiers for the Cinemetropolis Project. For $30, you can get the Cinemetropolis 2-LP vinyl, along with a free digital download of the album weeks before its official release date. For $70, you can get the vinyl along with that limited edition poster, CD, and the digital download.

We are fans of analog technology. Big fans. However, its production costs have risen as its consumer demand dwindles in this rapidly digitizing world. So the vinyl version’s first pressing will also be its last. There will be 500 vinyl copies made, and once they’re gone, they’re gone forever!

Last night, we played a few tracks on Cinemetropolis on KEXP’s Street Sounds (shoutout to Mr. Lar Mizell Jr.), and also dropped the official release date of the album is: June 14th. Don’t sleep! And in case you missed it, you can hear the live on-air interview and Cinemetropolis track previews at KEXP.org. Hit up the KEXP streaming archive and set the listen time to Sun, Mar. 27, 2011 at around 8 p.m.

item.title: The CINEMETROPOLIS Listening Party, part 1
item.dc:creator: Geo
item.description: A couple Sundays ago, we unveiled the 15 new tracks off Cinemetropolis at a listening party with fam in Seattle.
item.content:encoded:
A couple Sundays ago, we unveiled the 15 new tracks off Cinemetropolis at a listening party with fam in Seattle. It was a homecoming and reunion for us, as it was held at the Theater Off Jackson upstairs room, formerly the old Wing Luke Asian Museum, where I worked from 2002-2006 — the first four years of Blue Scholars’s existence. It was there that we finally announced who we decided to sign with for our next record, officially launching the Cinemetropolis campaign with new music and videos to drop in the weeks leading up to the album’s May digital release and June physical release.

Shoutout to Greg Nissen, who took these filthy photos (except, of course, the one he’s in at the bottom of this page). Hit up Greg’s tumblr for more photos from the listening party and check out what Guerilla Candy, Seattle Show Gal, and The Stranger have to say bout the party and first impressions of the new record.

item.title: The Hip Hop Word Count: Blue Scholars Approved
item.dc:creator: Hollis
item.description: We wanted to let everyone know about this proposed project, The Hip Hop Word Count: A Searchable Rap Almanac, that takes being a hip-hop head to brainiac status. This guy Tahir Hemphill is the mastermind behind the project,… More
item.content:encoded:
We wanted to let everyone know about this proposed project, The Hip Hop Word Count: A Searchable Rap Almanac, that takes being a hip-hop head to brainiac status. This guy Tahir Hemphill is the mastermind behind the project, which he describes thusly:

How can analyzing lyrics teach us about our culture?

The Hip-Hop Word Count locks in a time and geographic location for every metaphor, simile, cultural reference, phrase, meme and socio-political idea used in the corpus of Hip-Hop.

The Hip-Hop Word Count then converts this data into explorable visualisations which help us to comprehend this vast set of cultural data.

This data can be used to chart the migration of ideas and builds a geography of language and is the engine for a teaching curriculum.

As students, we learn that cultures are remembered and live on through how they’re documented, be it oral tradition, historical record, or otherwise. Hip-hop as a culture has its own documentation: its lyricism. Often times, academic takes on hip-hop forgo its own self-expression and context, with a anthropological, subjective and theory-heavy approach that zaps the authenticity out of the account. This is the genius of this project: a top-level, thorough and accessible platform to let rap lyrics– and hip-hop– speak for themselves, with infinite possibilities as to how it’s applied.

As of this writing, the project needs only $2,000 more to become reality. If you got the guap, consider donating to this project. And you might even get a cool, tasty Rap Chocolate out of it.
